summary: Traces the male-supremacist online manosphere from Playboy and the 1970s men's rights movement through the 1989 Montreal massacre, pickup artistry, Vox Day's alpha-to-sigma hierarchy and Elliot Rodger's 2014 killings, then examines the sigma male self-help subculture.

evidence.note: men's liberation movement of the 1960s and its 1970s split into men's rights activism
Hefner's 1953 Playboy framed as the first break from 1950s manhood, anti-wife and anti-alimony
Lepine biography begins, leading to the 1989 Montreal engineering school shooting
survivor's account of the classroom shooting; manifesto read at length afterwards
Montreal attack described as the first incel terrorist attack, placing CA first in setting
The Game (2005) spreads pickup artistry through online forums, start of the core period
Vox Day segment: alt-right author, Holocaust denial, Return of Kings ties
Vox Day's 2010 blog post laying out the alpha-to-sigma male hierarchy
Rodger finds PUAHate in 2013; 2014 Isla Vista killing spree and its legacy
sigma male YouTube videos selling paid transformation courses

notes: Part 2 reads a self-published sigma male book and watches YouTube videos, so media-reading was considered; deep-dive chosen because part 1 (about two thirds of the story) is narrative history. covered_span starts with the 1953 Playboy segment, which together with men's liberation forms a real block. Japanese otaku culture is a comparison, so JP is left out.
